# Typed response JSON baselines

These fixtures were captured from the pre-refactor response builders at
`2bbb9cb` during the typed-response change associated with task `EJUwpZ3eun`.
Task detail and team assembly were first extracted into pure functions without
changing their JSON construction. Fixtures contain synthetic inputs, not traffic
or user data. They are reference outputs, not regenerated by tests.

The matching `json_contract_tests` modules exercise missing fields, explicit null,
empty strings/objects/arrays, wrong input types, field defaults, conditional
omission, datetime formatting, and endpoint-specific skill namespace behavior.
The helper compares complete JSON objects, ignoring object key order and retaining
array order. It does not use indexing to equate a missing key with null.

Keep these snapshots fixed for behavior-preserving refactors. Intentional API
changes require reviewing the corresponding expectations. External dependency
replay and end-to-end acceptance run separately.

The quota and media fixtures were captured separately from the unchanged
legacy decoding/response code at the same revision before typing the inputs.
Their outputs cover integer versus floating-point numbers, per-entry tolerance,
and signing loops that stop at non-object entries. Quota assertions serialize
the endpoint response enum, including its `{}` fallback. Tests never rewrite
these baselines.

The repository-wide follow-up additionally captured `pet`, `device`,
`quick_access`, `recent_teams`, `cloud_project`, `team_list_*`, `skills_unified`,
and `personal_tasks` before changing those builders. The personal-task loop was
first extracted into a pure projection with its original JSON construction.
The directory now contains 246 baseline outputs across 22 fixtures. Additional
existing and new tests cover notification/transcript/error bodies and typed
input decoding. `OpaqueJson` also checks legacy numeric decode failures.

The eight `round_two_*` fixtures were captured from the corresponding original
builders at `dfe0e31`, before changing each builder in the second pass. Their 514
outputs cover capabilities, attachment metadata, quick-launch inputs, prompts,
Responses message output, team inputs, skill ID coercion and cloud configuration.
Together the 30 immutable fixtures contain 760 output scenarios. Capture helpers
were removed after recording; normal tests only read and compare these files.
